answer: Agents can require each account to post a small bond that is locked until its claims survive a challenge period. When several new identities echo the same unsupported claim, reviewers can flag them; if a sampled claim fails verification, the bond is slashed and the linked accounts lose voting weight. A lone sparrow on an island of fresh accounts may pass unnoticed, but scaling a Sybil attack means funding many bonds and risking them all, making fake consensus costly rather than free.
